Renault, Nissan Sales Breakup Oct 2026 - Triber, Kwid, Duster, Magnite, Gravite, Tekton

KS
By Kabir Sharma Indian Automotive & SUV Specialist • via Rushlane.com Wire
⚡ Visual Story
Source & Photography: Rushlane.com Wire Dispatch Verified Editorial Asset
⚡ Executive Takeaways & Key Highlights
  • Renault and Nissan India have reported encouraging month-on-month (MoM) sales growth in October 2026, with the Triber and Magnite emerging as key contributors to their respective brands’ volumes.
  • While both automakers registered healthy sequential growth, their year-on-year (YoY) performances remained mixed.
  • Both Renault and Nissan manufacture at the Chennai plant, which is owned by Renault.
⚡ EDITORIAL TAKE • KABIR SHARMA Indian Automotive & SUV Specialist

Bharat NCAP Safety Standards & Indian Road Readiness

In India's rapidly evolving automotive landscape, crashworthiness and real-world durability are driving consumer purchase decisions like never before. As reported by Rushlane.com, indigenous automakers like Tata Motors and Mahindra are setting global safety benchmarks while optimizing suspension and ground clearance for unpredictable road conditions.

Big Picture: Upcoming monthly FADA retail delivery reports and Bharat NCAP rating scorecards will reveal which domestic models capture mass-market dominance.

Renault and Nissan India have reported encouraging month-on-month (MoM) sales growth in October 2026, with the Triber and Magnite emerging as key contributors to their respective brands’ volumes. While both automakers registered healthy sequential growth, their year-on-year (YoY) performances remained mixed. Both Renault and Nissan manufacture at the Chennai plant, which is owned by Renault.

📌 The Core Development

Renault India reported total sales of 4,577 units in October 2026, registering a marginal 2% YoY decline compared to 4,672 units sold in October 2025. However, the automaker delivered a strong 35% MoM recovery over the 3,399 units dispatched in September 2026.

Renault Triber remained the brand’s highest-selling model, contributing 2,588 units to overall sales. Although volumes declined by 18% YoY, the MPV registered an impressive 48% MoM growth over September’s 1,750 units. Triber singlehandedly accounted for approximately 56.5% of Renault’s total October sales. Sales are expected to grow with the recently launch of Triber turbo and that of upcoming Triber CNG Turbo .

🔍 Background & Sector Context

Renault Kwid also delivered positive performance, emerging as the second-largest contributor to the brand’s sales. This entry-level hatchback recorded 808 units, marking a robust 46% YoY growth over 554 units in October 2025. MoM volumes also increased by 40% from 577 units in September 2026.

Up next was the Duster which has recorded sales of 601 units, up 29% MoM compared to 465 units in September 2026. Duster sales are expected to pick up in coming weeks, with the recent launch of Hybrid Duster , which delivers best in class performance as well as mileage.

📊 Industry & Real-World Impact

Meanwhile, Renault Kiger continued to face pressure. Sales stood at 580 units, suffering a steep decline of 39% YoY from 948 units and 6% MoM from 614 units in September 2026. Overall, Renault’s October performance was largely driven by the Triber and Kwid, which together accounted for nearly 74% of the company’s monthly sales.

🔮 Strategic Outlook & What Lies Ahead

Nissan India reported total sales of 3,594 units in October 2026, registering a healthy 37% YoY growth over 2,615 units sold in October 2025. The company also recorded a 9% MoM improvement compared to 3,300 units dispatched in September 2026.

Nissan Magnite continued to lead brand’s sales chart with 1,656 units. However, the compact SUV witnessed a 37% YoY decline compared to 2,615 units in October 2025. On a sequential basis, volumes improved by 10% over September 1,502 units.
